title: The seven bridges of Königsberg
learningObjective: Discover why four odd-degree vertices prevent an Euler walk.

social.title: MiniMundos · The Seven Bridges of Königsberg
social.description: Can you cross every bridge exactly once? Enter a tiny historical world and discover the idea that began graph theory.
social.imageAlt: MiniMundos miniature map of Königsberg, with seven bridges connecting four areas of land.

atlas.title: Seven bridges. One impossible walk?
atlas.question: Can you cross every bridge exactly once?
atlas.description: Wander a river city, trace your own route, and discover the deceptively simple puzzle that opened a new branch of mathematics.
atlas.imageAlt: The playable miniature Königsberg: a river city of tree-lined islands, terracotta roofs and wooden bridges.

title: The curve of fastest descent
learningObjective: Discover why the quickest descent is not the shortest path.

social.title: MiniMundos · The Brachistochrone
social.description: Shape a wooden track, release three riders together, and discover the curve of fastest descent.

atlas.title: The fastest way isn’t the straightest.
atlas.question: Which curve wins the race to the bottom?
atlas.description: Step into an imagined workshop inspired by Bernoulli’s 1696 challenge. Shape a track, release the riders, and put your intuition to the test.
atlas.imageAlt: The playable miniature workshop with curved racing tracks, a waterwheel, and a wooded landscape.

title: The Monty Hall problem
learningObjective: Discover why switching wins more often when a knowledgeable host reveals the goats.

social.title: MiniMundos · The Monty Hall Problem
social.description: Enter a 1975 television studio. Choose a door, meet the goats, and discover why switching changes your chances.
social.imageAlt: An original miniature 1970s television studio with three prize doors, a host, cameras and a costumed audience.

atlas.title: The door you didn’t choose.
atlas.question: Would you keep your door, or switch?
atlas.description: You’re on the air in an imagined 1975 studio. Pick a door, let the host reveal the goats, and test your intuition. Then go backstage, pull the lever, and ride a lift through a right-triangle studio of up to 55 doors.
atlas.imageAlt: The playable miniature Monty Hall studio: colourful closed doors, warm marquee bulbs, television cameras and a costumed audience.

title: Young Gauss and the hundred numbers
learningObjective: Discover the pairing pattern behind 1 + 2 + … + 100 and prove the sum of the first n positive integers.

social.title: MiniMundos · Young Gauss
social.description: Look through a magnifier at a classroom full of arithmetic and discover one elegant idea.
social.imageAlt: A miniature schoolroom with wooden desks and students working on chalk slates.

atlas.title: A hundred numbers. One little idea.
atlas.question: Can you find a shortcut hiding in the numbers?
atlas.description: Visit an imagined schoolroom of young Gauss. Inspect the students’ slates with a magnifier, compare their methods, and discover how pairing the ends turns a hundred numbers into one elegant calculation.
atlas.imageAlt: The playable miniature Gauss classroom with six pupils, wooden desks, tall windows, and a chalkboard arithmetic challenge.
